summary: This program builds a small glossary using a Map, where each Java collection name is a key paired with its definition. It looks up one definition by name, then copies the keys into a TreeSet so the terms can be listed in alphabetical order.

lines.text: TreeSet is imported alongside the map classes because it keeps its contents sorted, which is what makes the alphabetical listing possible.
The variable is declared as the Map interface but created as a HashMap; both type parameters are String because a term and its definition are each text.

lines.code: glossary.put("List", "An ordered collection (also known as a sequence) that may contain duplicate elements. Allows positional access and insertion of elements.");
lines.text: put stores a key-value pair, so the term "List" becomes the key you look up and the definition becomes the value you get back.
Holding the search term in a variable means the lookup and the printed label always agree, and you change the search in one place.
get returns the value stored under that key, or null if the term was never added to the glossary.
The \n escape sequence starts a new line before the heading, which separates the two sections of output visually.
keySet gives you all the terms in the map, and passing them to a TreeSet constructor copies them into sorted order — a HashMap on its own has no reliable ordering.
Iterating over a TreeSet visits the elements smallest to largest, so the terms come out alphabetically without any sorting code of your own.
